To find the electrostatic (interaction) energy when a point charge q is placed at a distance d ( d > R ) from the centre of a grounded conducting sphere of radius R, use the method of images.

1. Replace the sphere by an image charge  
   q′ = −q (R/d)  
   located on the same line at a distance  
   a = R²/d  
   from the centre.

2. The only real charge is q.  
   The potential energy is one‐half the real charge multiplied by the potential at its position produced by everything else (i.e. by the image charge only):

   U = ½ q V_image(at q)
     = ½  k  q q′ / |d − a|.

3. Insert q′ and a:

   |d − a| = d − R²/d = (d² − R²)/d,

   U = ½  k  q [−q (R/d)] / [(d² − R²)/d]
     = −½  k  q² R/d · d/(d² − R²)
     = −½  k  q² R /(d² − R²).

Thus the net potential energy is  

U = − (1/2) k q² R /(d² − R²).

Answer: D
